sections.h2: How can I sell my house in Lebanon, TN?
sections.html:
Lebanon homeowners can use an agent, sell directly to a buyer they find, or take an as-is cash offer. Pick based on the shape of the house, your deadline and how much of the sale price you are willing to give up for speed.

Lebanon has grown quickly. The Census Bureau estimates 53,412 residents on July 1, 2025, a 38.8% jump over the April 2020 base of 38,495. Owners occupy 62.4% of housing units, the median owner-occupied value is $378,400 and median gross rent is $1,306.

  • A listing exposes the house to the most buyers but follows the buyer's inspection and loan timeline.
  • A private sale saves the agent fee and puts the paperwork on you.
  • A cash offer removes showings and repairs and lets you set the closing date.

sections.h2: What is Lebanon, Tennessee like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lebanon is the county seat of Wilson County, about 25 miles east of downtown Nashville, and it was incorporated in 1801, according to Wikipedia. Locals call it Cedar City after the red cedars that grow in the area. Cumberland University, founded in 1842, and the Nashville Superspeedway are two landmarks, and the Tennessee State Fair is held here with the Wilson County Fair.

Commuters shape demand. Interstate 40 runs south of the city with three Lebanon exits, U.S. 70 leads west to Nashville, and the WeGo Star commuter train ends in Lebanon with weekday service. Hartmann Drive and Maddox-Simpson Parkway form a partial beltway, and the Census Bureau puts mean travel time to work at 27.0 minutes.

sections.h2: What drives the local economy in Lebanon?
sections.html:
Several large employers sit inside the city. Cracker Barrel was founded in Lebanon in 1969 and keeps its headquarters here, and Lochinvar, a water products maker, is also based in town. The Wonderful Group invested $150 million in a tile plant in 2015, its first manufacturing site in North America, and Tritium opened an electric vehicle fast-charger plant in 2022.

The Census Bureau reports retail sales of about $3.48 billion in 2022 and a median household income of $72,848 for 2020-2024.

sections.h2: Which schools serve a Lebanon address?
sections.html:
Lebanon Special School District covers most of the city for pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. Its Director of Schools page reports about 4,600 students, five elementary schools (Byars Dowdy, Castle Heights, Coles Ferry, Jones Brummett and Sam Houston) and two middle schools, Walter J. Baird and Winfree Bryant.

High school students are zoned to Wilson County Schools, which also serves a few small parts of Lebanon for all grades. District lines decide a buyer's school, so tell buyers to confirm an address with the district and not rely on a listing description. LSSD offers an address search tool on its own site.

sections.h2: Does Lebanon's weather matter when preparing a house for sale?
sections.html:
Lebanon has a humid subtropical climate. Wikipedia's NOAA-based table shows the average July high at 90.2 degrees, about 54 inches of precipitation a year across roughly 117 wet days, and only 1.5 inches of snow in a typical year. The record high is 111 degrees and the record low is minus 20.

That pattern puts the stress on roofs, gutters, grading and cooling equipment more than on freeze damage. Before you accept or reject an offer, a roof and drainage check tells you what a buyer's inspector is likely to raise.

sections.h2: How do Lebanon city and Wilson County property taxes work?
sections.html:
Lebanon taxes each house once for the city and once for Wilson County, and the two bills have different payment points. The City of Lebanon lists a rate of $0.4054 per $100 of assessed value, collected at the city property tax office at 200 N. Castle Heights Avenue.

Lebanon and Wilson County tax calendar (City of Lebanon and Wilson County Assessor)
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date for all property
May 20Assessor notes assessments on the roll and notifies owners of changes
June 1County Board of Equalization begins hearing appeals
August 1State Board of Equalization appeal deadline, or 45 days after the county result if later
October 1 to February 28City taxes payable without penalty
March 1City penalty starts at 1.5% per month

The Wilson County Assessor values the property and the state prints the notices, so address corrections go to the assessor at 615-444-8661. County bills go out in mid-October, and the Wilson County Trustee at 228 E. Main Street, Room 102 takes payment through the end of February.

sections.h2: What can a Lebanon owner do about a high assessment before selling?
sections.html:
Start with a call or visit to the Wilson County Property Assessor, because many disputes are clerical. The assessor's appeal page says the next step is the County Board of Equalization, a panel of five property owners with one seat from Lebanon, one from Mt. Juliet and three from the county.

The board sits from June 1 until that year's work is done, and the assessor publishes a newspaper notice about ten days ahead. Appointments are normally requested by phone or in person in the last week of May or the first week of June. You may appear yourself, send a relative or attorney, and bring witnesses. A lower assessed value helps the next owner, so pursue the appeal before you list if the number looks wrong.

sections.h2: Who handles permits, short-term rentals and building rules in Lebanon?
sections.html:
The city's planning and building departments split the work. Zoning enforcement officials handle pools, fences, sidewalks and short-term rental permits, and they also staff the Board of Zoning Appeals for setback variances and accessory structure variances, per the Long Range Planning page. Zoning staff also support the Historic Zoning Commission, which handles certificates of appropriateness.

  • Building permits and inspections come from the Chief Building Official's staff, who hold ICC and state certifications.
  • Electrical inspections are not done by the city. State of Tennessee deputy electrical inspectors do them.
  • New single-family and townhome projects follow a five-step residential development process before a certificate of occupancy is issued.

If you plan to sell a house that was rented to short-term guests, call the zoning office at 615-444-3647 and ask what permit is on file.

sections.h2: How is a Lebanon sale recorded?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Wilson County Register of Deeds, and the state's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, per the Tennessee Department of Revenue. On a $378,400 sale, which matches the city's Census median, that tax would be $1,400.

Owners over 65 or disabled may have state and county tax relief, and seniors may qualify for the tax freeze on a primary residence, both run by the Wilson County Trustee at 615-444-0894 (option 2). Ask the Trustee how a sale during the year affects either program.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lebanon house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer a copy of the lease up front and ask the title company how it affects the closing. A buyer who purchases as-is can take a rented house, and the tenant's plans can be settled in the contract.

faqs.q: When are Lebanon city property taxes due?
faqs.a: City taxes are payable from October 1 through February 28. Penalty at 1.5% per month starts accruing March 1, according to the City of Lebanon.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Lebanon house for tax purposes?
faqs.a: The Wilson County Property Assessor does. The city applies its own rate to that value, and appeals go first to the assessor and then to the County Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Is there a tax freeze for older Lebanon homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The Wilson County Trustee runs a tax freeze for owners 65 and older that holds the tax amount on a primary residence, along with a relief program for older, disabled and disabled veteran owners. Call 615-444-0894 and choose option 2.

faqs.q: Does the city inspect electrical work on a Lebanon house?
faqs.a: No. Electrical inspections are done by State of Tennessee deputy inspectors, not by the Lebanon Building Inspection Department.
